Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Effusion, left knee; lateral left knee pain with clicking for 5 months after twisting knee injury
Comparison: Left knee radiograph [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Minimal fraying along the patella. No focal trochlear cartilage defects.  

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Minimal patellar chondrosis. Otherwise, no intra-articular injury.

[DATE]: MR Knie Links 15ch AA: Klinische inlichtingen: Zie gescande aanvraag Diagnostische vraagstelling: Zie gescande aanvraag Bevindingen: Volledige scheur van de voorste kruisband, proximale 3e, met onderbreking vezels, infiltratie intercondylaire notch,. Slechts minimale opzetting van suprapatellaire recessus. Licht verdikt voorkomen mediaal collateraal ligament, met vochtinfiltratie oppervlakkig en diep aan het ligament. Beperkt botoedeem posterieur op het mediale tibiaplateau. Incomplete verticale scheur posterieure hoorn mediale meniscus. Beginnend tot gevorderd femoropatellair kraakbeenlijden, gekenmerkt door multipele fissuren, langs schuine fissuur met flapvorming op de mediale facet, en kleine geode's met beperkt botoedeem op het laterale facet van de patella. Kleine popliteale cyste. Uitgebreid subcutaan oedeem, posterieure helft dijbeen. Besluit: Ernstige distorsio van de linkerknie met: - v olledige ruptuur van de voorste kruisband; - p arti ële scheur mediaal collateraal ligament ; - i ncomplete verticale scheur perifeer op de posterieure hoorn van de mediale meniscus . Voorafbestaand matig tot gevorderd femoropatellair kraakbeenlijden .

FINDINGS:

There is a small knee joint effusion with no popliteal cysts.

There are moderate degenerative changes in the medial compartment with moderate cartilage thinning most pronounced at the central weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is diffuse mild thinning and superficial fraying in the lateral and patellofemoral compartments. There are no regions of full-thickness cartilage loss.

There is intrasubstance degeneration involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a longitudinal oblique tear involving the posterior horn extending to the inferior articular surface. There is an intra and para meniscal cyst at the level of the posterior root. There is no displaced meniscal fragment. The lateral meniscus is unremarkable.

Otherwise the anterior cruciate ligament, the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Mild to moderate degenerative changes most pronounced in the medial compartment as detailed above. No evidence of intra-articular body.

2. Intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus with an oblique tear and para meniscal cyst. No displaced meniscal fragment.

3. Knee joint effusion with no popliteal cysts.

MRI of left  Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc LT, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS

> Mild laxity contour of MCL  and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneration or grade 1 injury.
> The contour of ACL, PCL and LCL within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Osteoarthritis of left knee joint with spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema/cysts in patella and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage, major in patellofemoral joint and medial femorotibial joint.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and thick medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over anterior aspect of left knee.
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O paratendinitis.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at medial patellofemoral joint with grade 4 chondromalacia..
2. Degneraiton of meniscus and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and thick medial patellar retinaculum.
4. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of MCL; R/O paratendinitis of pes anserinus.
5. Subcutaneous edema over anterior aspect of left knee.
